Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web

Class ProblemJsonExceptionHandler

java.lang.Object
org.springframework.web.servlet.mvc.method.annotation.ResponseEntityExceptionHandler
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.ProblemJsonExceptionHandler
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.springframework.beans.factory.Aware, org.springframework.context.MessageSourceAware
Direct Known Subclasses:
AccountExceptionHandler, ClientExceptionHandler, MfaExceptionHandler, OttExceptionHandler, PasskeyExceptionHandler
public class ProblemJsonExceptionHandler extends org.springframework.web.servlet.mvc.method.annotation.ResponseEntityExceptionHandler
Base of the exception handlers of the REST API: every problem detail is answered as application/problem+json (RFC 9457), as the contracts under apis/ declare.

The interfaces generated from a contract map each operation with the media types it produces, for example application/json and application/problem+json. Spring MVC keeps those as the producible types of an error answer too and, for a client that accepts anything, would pick the first one: a problem detail would then go out as application/json. Setting the content type of every problem answer keeps the contract's media type whatever the order of the generated list.

It is not an advice itself: each feature declares its own @RestControllerAdvice extending it, scoped to its controller.
